results.test: user sees the correct total including discount and VAT
results.fixerReasoning: The app's own business rules in public/cart.js (rule 3) say VAT is charged on the amount after the discount, and the test case says the same. But `vat()` computes `taxable = subtotal(items)`, so it taxes the full 1398 instead of 1258. That gives round(1398 × 0.21) = 294 instead of round(1258 × 0.21) = 264, which is exactly the value received. The test is correct and is catching a real bug, so the test must not be changed.
results.fixerReport: The VAT calculation in public/cart.js is wrong. `vat()` uses `const taxable = subtotal(items);` but the documented rule is that VAT is charged after the discount. It should be `const taxable = subtotal(items) - discount(items);`. As a result, every order over 1000 is overcharged: on the 1398 basket in this test, VAT shows 294 instead of 264 and the total comes to 1552 instead of 1522 (an overcharge of 30). The fix belongs in the app, not the test. Leave tests/cart.spec.js:56 failing until the app is fixed. Two things for a human to confirm: (1) that rule 3 (VAT after discount) is still the intended rule, and (2) whether a release has already overcharged real customers. Unrelated, but noticed: data/products.json lists the desk mat (id 4) at 349, while the 'catalogue price' test and its test case expect 299. That is a separate data-drift question someone needs to decide on.

results.test: user sees the whole catalogue once it has loaded
results.fixerReasoning: The app is behaving as documented: public/index.html renders the first four products, then deliberately adds the fifth 1500 ms later. The test case's own preconditions say the last rows can arrive late. The test waits a fixed 100 ms and then takes a one-off count(), so it reads 4 every time. The test is the problem, not the app or the data. Replacing the sleep and the count with Playwright's auto-retrying toHaveCount(5) fixes it, because that assertion keeps checking for up to the default 5 s expect timeout. It still fails if the app never renders all five products.
results.reviewerReasoning: I checked the claim against public/index.html. The page renders products.slice(0, 4) first and adds the fifth row in a setTimeout of 1500 ms, under a comment saying the catalogue is paged. The test case's preconditions also say 'the last rows can arrive late'. So the app works as specified. The test fails because it sleeps a fixed 100 ms and then takes a single count(), which can only ever see 4 rows. toHaveCount(5) waits for the condition the test case describes, with the default 5 s expect timeout and a 10 s test timeout. It still requires exactly five rows, so it would fail if the fifth product never rendered, or if a sixth showed up.
